chunks: "The wiping of the head is upon its front part."

If someone says: It has already appeared in your discourse that wiping over the feet is the obligation, while your opponents reject you on that and say that this is an innovation, and that the obligation is washing rather than wiping—then what is your proof against them? It is said to him: Our proof against them is His, Exalted is He, saying:
"O you who believe! When you rise for salat (prayer), wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles."

So the verse explicitly states two rulings regarding two limbs. Then it coordinates the hands with the faces, thereby making their ruling, by means of coordination, like their ruling; and it coordinates the feet with the heads, thereby making it necessary that they share with them the same ruling of wiping by virtue of the coordination. If it were permissible for their ruling to differ despite the coordination, then it would also be permissible for their ruling regarding the faces to differ. This is also indicated by the following.

What al-Shaykh—may Allah, Exalted is He, support him—informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abi Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

1-172-21 — What has been narrated from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام and Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله that he performed wudu (ablution) and wiped over his feet and his sandals.

key_terms.الرِّجْلَيْنِ: the two feet as the limb discussed in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْعَطْفِ: grammatical coordination used as the basis of the legal argument

ai.seo_question: What is the proof that the feet are wiped, not washed, in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This passage argues, on the basis of Qur'anic grammar, that the obligation in wudu (ablution) concerning the feet is wiping rather than washing. It supports this interpretation by linking "your feet" to "your heads" in the verse of wudu and then citing a prophetic tradition describing the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله as wiping over his feet.
